specs.title: CSV export of the reports page
sources: request ps-013 from the owner, CSV export part; one spec per deliverable line (skills-plan rule)
in_scope: the reports page offers a CSV download of the report the user is viewing
non_goals: the partner REST API (separate line, separate spec)
any change to what the reports show

criteria.text: Given a user on the reports page with a report loaded, when the user chooses Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads whose rows and columns match the on-screen report.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the file with the on-screen data for a fixed dataset.

criteria.text: Given a report with no rows, when the user chooses Export CSV, then the result is the behaviour set in open question 2.
criteria.check: Negative test with an empty dataset, written once open question 2 is answered.

open_questions.question: Which rows does the export contain?

options.option: the rows of the current filtered view
all rows of the report regardless of view
options.changes: criterion 1 widens to the full report

open_questions.question: What does the export do when the report is empty?

options.option: a file with the header row only
options.changes: criterion 2 is a file with no data rows

options.option: a message instead of a file

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: request ps-013 from the owner, partner API part; one spec per deliverable line
in_scope: a public REST endpoint that returns the same reports the CSV export shows
non_goals: the CSV export on the reports page (separate line)

criteria.text: Given a partner with valid access, when it requests a report, then it receives the same rows and columns the reports page shows for that report.
criteria.check: API integration test against the fixed dataset, once open question 1 fixes the access model.

criteria.text: Given a request without valid access, when it is made, then the API refuses it and returns no report data.
criteria.check: Negative API test, written once open question 1 is answered.

open_questions.question: How do partners authenticate, and which reports may each partner read?

options.option: one API key per partner with a report scope
OAuth client credentials with per-partner scopes
options.changes: criteria 1 and 2 use token checks and add a scope check

open_questions.waiting_for: owner; this is a security and privacy decision, so it is escalated

open_questions.question: Are there rate limits for partners at launch?

options.option: none at launch
a fixed per-partner limit

actions_now: Write two separate draft specs, one per branch, with the access model and the export scope left as open questions for the owner. The partner API spec is escalated because access to report data is a security and privacy decision.
